item.title: An exact computer-assisted lower bound for Fisher-information convexity along the two-dimensional heat flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.20653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the sharp constant in the differential inequality \[ I(t)I''(t)\geq c\,[I'(t)]^2 \] for Fisher information along the probability-normalized heat flow on $\mathbb R^2$. The unrestricted log-convexity value $c=1$ is false in two dimensions, whereas the known square-root convexity theorem gives the universal value $c=1/2$. We construct an exact, machine-verifiable sum-of-squares certificate proving the stronger universal bound \[ c\geq \frac{231691}{250000}=0.926764. \] Together with an independent exact Fourier/Gaussian-envelope construction, this gives \[ 0.926764\leq c_*<0.94176665012062, \] where $c_*$ is the sharp constant for positive-time Gaussian convolutions of arbitrary probability measures on $\mathbb R^2$. We formulate the proof in explicit two-dimensional index notation. The lower bound follows from an exact rational polynomial identity involving a strictly positive denominator, a weighted total derivative, and eleven positive rational Gram matrices. All $491$ recorded leading principal minors are strictly positive and the complete polynomial identity has zero residual. No symmetry, log-concavity, finite-variance, or finite-entropy assumption is imposed on the initial measure. The sharp value remains open.
item.dc:creator: Fayez Abu-Ajamieh, Xiaoyan Huo

item.title: Analog RF Computing for Integrated Data and AI Flows Over Wireless Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.20841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many resource-constrained edge devices require artificial intelligence (AI) services but are not powerful enough to store or execute neural networks (NNs). Analog radio frequency (RF) computing addresses this limitation by letting a base station (BS) multicast a waveform encoding NN weights to different clients. Each client then multiplies the received weight-encoded waveform with its locally generated input-encoded waveform through a passive mixer in its RF frontend, thereby realizing the matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) needed for AI inference with an extremely low power and memory requirement. This can enable telecom operators to provide AI inference services to the edge devices connected to their networks. In practice, however, this multicast AI flow must share the spectrum, power, and spatial resources with other data flows. This paper considers a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) downlink scenario and studies the resulting relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating the multicast AI flow with the unicast data flows. We formulate a joint beamforming problem for the data and AI flows to maximize the aggregate data rate subject to computing accuracy, client energy, total power, and hardware-related constraints. We develop a weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE)-based algorithm to solve the problem. Numerical results based on 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) channels show that the relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating an AI flow with data flows is below 5% in representative settings. This indicates that telecom operators can use analog RF computing to provide edge AI services while providing data communication services simultaneously.
item.dc:creator: Wentao Yu, Vincent W. S. Wong

item.title: LWM-TF: A Wireless Foundation Model on 5G NR Time-Frequency Resource Grids
item.description: arXiv:2610.21013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Received OFDM grids preserve both pilot and payload observations, yet wireless foundation models are rarely pre-trained on them. We introduce LWM-TF, a 9.58M-parameter factorized masked autoencoder pre-trained on complex 5G NR uplink grids taken after the FFT and before channel estimation. Each block attends first across OFDM symbols and then across resource blocks and receive antennas, and the mask follows the same two axes. Because the payload phase is unpredictable, the model reconstructs the normalized log-power of each masked token and predicts its scale separately; ablations show that the two terms are complementary and that this target outperforms complex-signal reconstruction. The encoder is pre-trained on 850,496 physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) slots from a 10^6-slot dataset simulated with the NR transmit chain under various channel conditions. With the encoder frozen, linear probes classify modulation, predict CRC success, and detect UE mobility. On a separately generated test set, 16 labeled slots per class give 0.85 modulation accuracy, 0.82 CRC area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and 0.73 mobility AUROC, ahead of a supervised CNN on every paired draw. With 10,000 labels the probes reach 0.94, 0.96, and 0.92, well above engineered receiver statistics, and detect mobility where the CNN stays at chance. Without any impairment labels, distances in the frozen feature space flag unseen waveform impairments with 0.78 macro AUROC, against 0.68 for receiver statistics. A single pre-trained encoder thus provides receiver features that transfer across tasks, most strongly when labels are scarce.
item.dc:creator: Namhyun Kim, Sadjad Alikhani, Ahmed Alkhateeb

item.title: Superfast Spectral Compressed Sensing with Quadratic Convergence
item.description: arXiv:2610.21068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the spectral compressed sensing problem of recovering a spectrally sparse signal from linear compressive measurements. Exploiting the low-rank Hankel structure associated with the signal, we formulate a nonconvex fixed-rank optimization problem with a Hankel regularization. We propose a Superfast Iterative Hard Thresholding (SIHT) algorithm, where each iteration consists of a tangent-space least-squares update followed by a fixed-rank hard thresholding projection. SIHT is the first nonconvex algorithm with provable quadratic convergence for spectral compressed sensing. For random Gaussian measurements, it achieves exact recovery in the noiseless case and stable recovery in the noisy case with near-optimal sample complexity. To efficiently implement SIHT, we develop a parameterized conjugate gradient method for solving the least-squares subproblem, endowing SIHT with state-of-the-art computational and memory efficiency. Numerical experiments are provided to validate our results.
item.dc:creator: Xunmeng Wu, Jian-Feng Cai, Zongben Xu, Zai Yang

item.title: Four-Level Quantized Soft Information Aided Hard-Decision Decoder for Product-like Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.21187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a novel low-complexity soft-aided hard-decision decoding scheme for product-like codes, termed iterative bounded-distance decoding (iBDD) with graded scaled reliability and bit-flipping (GSRF). This scheme operates on four-level quantized soft information. It incorporates a graded scaled reliability rule to assign decoding confidence to the bounded-distance decoding result, and employs a bit-flipping rule based on bit-level and component-code-level reliability. A selective re-decoding rule is designed to further facilitate the error performance while keeping the number of BDD attempts in reasonably low levels. The decoding parameter design of iBDD-GSRF is investigated for product codes and staircase codes, respectively. Simulation results on both codes verify that iBDD-GSRF achieves a gain of more than 0.4 dB over the conventional iBDD, comparable to several existing unquantized soft-aided decoders.
item.dc:creator: Xiaowei Wu, Min Qiu, Yueying Zhan, Lei Yang

item.title: On the Subadditivity of Mutual f-Information
item.description: arXiv:2610.21231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address an open problem raised by Polyanskiy and Wu in their textbook concerning the subadditivity of mutual \(f\)-information. We study two notions of generalized mutual information: mutual \(f\)-information, defined by \(\widetilde{I}_f(X;Y)=D_f(p_{XY}\|p_Xp_Y)\), and variational \((G,f)\)-information, obtained by minimizing an average of transformed \(f\)-divergences. For the first notion, we derive a sufficient condition on \(g(x)=x^2f''(x)\) that guarantees subadditivity under conditionally independent observations. This condition yields explicit families beyond the previously known examples generated by \(x\log x\) and \((x-1)\log x\). Our proof relies on the concavity of a generalized variance functional. For the variational notion, we extend existing sufficient conditions beyond the transforms \(G(x)\in\{x,\log(1+x),-\log(1-x)\}\). Using a comparison inequality for \(G^{-1}(G(A)+G(B))\), we obtain differential criteria for concave and convex transforms. Explicit constructions illustrate the resulting classes of subadditive information measures.
item.dc:creator: Hamidreza Abin, Amin Gohari

item.title: Iterative Bounded Distance Decoding With 2-Bit Reliability Marker For Product-Like Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.21279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a novel soft-aided hard-decision decoding scheme for product codes based on two-bit quantized reliability markers. In particular, one bit is used for a two-level tolerance miscorrection check to validate the bounded distance decoding (BDD) result, while the other identifies bits to be randomly flipped upon BDD failure and miscorrection. List decoding is incorporated to further facilitate the error performance. Density evolution is performed for the design of the quantization thresholds. Compared to iterative BDD, the proposed scheme requires only moderate increases in memory and computational overhead. Simulation results verify that our scheme outperforms several unquantized soft-aided decoders, while maintaining small memory costs and low BDD attempts.
item.dc:creator: Xiaowei Wu, Min Qiu, Yueying Zhan, Lei Yang

item.title: On the structure of polynomial ideal codes and additive Reed--Solomon codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.21509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study structural properties of polynomial ideal (PI) codes and additive Reed--Solomon (aRS) codes in the folded Hamming metric (equivalently, the Hamming metric over a larger alphabet). We first determine the maximum possible length of PI codes, prove that the dual of every PI code is a generalized PI code, and deduce that PI codes are dually QMDS together with an explicit formula for their weight distribution. We then show that PI codes defined by irreducible polynomials correspond to aRS codes with pairwise nonconjugate evaluation points. For these aRS codes, the previous results on PI codes apply (duality, QMDS property and weight distribution). We show that, asymptotically, aRS codes with nonconjugate evaluation points achieve the same length as PI codes. We also compute the permutation group of such aRS codes. We also extend the family of PI codes to consider arbitrary polynomial modules (not necessarily pairwise coprime), and study when these and general aRS codes satisfy the QMDS and dually QMDS properties.
item.dc:creator: Umberto Mart\'inez-Pe\~{n}as, Rub\'en Rodr\'iguez-Ballesteros

item.title: It Takes Two Moments: Rigidity and Limits of Continuous Encoders for Over-the-Air Computation
item.description: arXiv:2610.21536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study over-the-air computation of functions, such as empirical variance, formed by combining two separately postprocessed sums of locally transformed observations. We consider continuous encoders subject to pointwise peak-power constraints over a single use of a complex multiple-access channel. With four or more transmitters, we identify conditions under which exact noiseless recovery forces every continuous encoder collection into a common affine structure that preserves both sums, reducing infinite-dimensional encoder design to selecting a finite set of coefficients. To quantify resilience against channel noise, we introduce a robustness score that measures the separation of noiseless received aggregates relative to variations in the desired function value. Within this characterized encoder family, we formulate robustness maximization as an exact convex semi-infinite program, eliminating rank constraints without a relaxation gap, and construct a decoder that attains the minimum uniform noise-amplification constant. For several function classes, including empirical variance, we derive closed-form robustness-optimal encoders and scores. Under mild regularity conditions, we also establish sharp limits on the Gaussian mean squared error at high signal-to-noise ratios and show how using the input distribution reduces average error at the expense of uniform robustness.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Razavikia

item.title: How Does Probabilistic Constellation Shaping Control Ranging Sidelobe Levels in ISAC?
item.description: arXiv:2610.21653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Probabilistic constellation shaping (PCS), originally designed to fill the gap between finite uniform constellations and continuous capacity-achieving input distributions, has recently emerged as a central tool in adjusting the expected integrated sidelobe level (EISL) in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). In this paper, we show that PCS goes beyond EISL: A large class of PCS methods, termed as type-based PCS, are capable of providing precise control over codeword-wise integrated sidelobe level ratio (ISLR) for systems employing orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), thus yielding a stronger sensing performance guarantee than EISL control. We further show that OFDM is almost the only unitary modulation basis whose codeword-wise ISLR can be precisely controlled by type-based PCS. Based upon the analytical results, practical type-based PCS methods compatible with the probabilistic amplitude shaping (PAS) framework are conceived, which achieve higher communication rates than existing ISAC-oriented PCS methods under identical ISLR constraints.
item.dc:creator: Zexuan Jing, Yifeng Xiong, Fan Liu, Xuehua Li, Jianhua Zhang

item.title: Fisher Information and Support Complexity of Gaussian Mixtures
item.description: arXiv:2610.21726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study lower bounds on the Fisher information of Gaussian location mixtures and their applications to estimation problems. First, for a discrete mixing distribution, we derive a universal positive-semidefinite lower bound on the Fisher information matrix in terms of the R\'enyi entropy of order two. For a mixing distribution supported on $K$ points, this bound scales as $\log(K)/K^2$, improving by a logarithmic factor on the support-size dependence obtained from Stam's inequality. We then develop dimension-aware trace bounds using classical Sobolev inequalities. These bounds are expressed in terms of Sibson's $\alpha$-mutual information and yield the scaling $K^{-2/n}$ in dimension $n$. A complementary bound involving the $\alpha$-mutual information of order $1/2$ is obtained using the sharp Young convolution inequality. The derived inequalities are further specialized to rotationally invariant mixing distributions supported on discrete spherical shells. In this setting, an intrinsic-dimensional bound on Sibson mutual information leads to lower bounds on the Fisher information in terms of the number of occupied shells. As applications, we study least favorable priors for bounded Gaussian mean estimation. In the scalar case, we show that the least favorable prior on $[-R,R]$ has at least $\Omega(R\sqrt{\log R})$ support points and that each of its probability masses is of order at most $1/R$. In the vector case, we show that the number of occupied shells grows at least linearly with $R$. Finally, Brown's identity and the I-MMSE relationship are used to translate the Fisher-information inequalities into upper bounds on the MMSE and mutual information.
item.dc:creator: Luca Barletta, Alex Dytso

item.title: Short-Boundary Signaling for Asynchronous Grant-Free Control-to-Control Communications
item.description: arXiv:2610.21729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In asynchronous grant-free access, receivers must detect variable-length transmissions and identify their start and end. Existing decoder-aided receivers use start and tail sequences which are as long as one codeword, causing substantial overhead for short commands. This paper treats the boundary (i.e., start and tail sequences) length as an independent design parameter and proposes a convolutional neural network that detects both boundaries from the received waveform and the decoder soft output. Its waveform input size decreases with the boundary length, while the decoder input keeps the codeword length, so the boundary can be shortened without altering the decoder. Analysis and simulations quantify the resulting tradeoff among payload efficiency, collision exposure, and boundary detection. The results show that the proposed receiver can exploit very short boundaries: in the considered setting, the shortest tested boundary, $L_{\mathrm{b}}=16$, yields the highest effective payload efficiency at all tested loads, whereas a correlation-based benchmark with the same sequences performs best with $L_{\mathrm{b}}=64$ at moderate and high loads.
item.dc:creator: Massimo Battaglioni, Dania De Crescenzo, Edoardo Carnevali, Enrico Paolini

item.title: Model-Driven Deep Learning for Distributed Detection with Low-Bit Quantization
item.description: arXiv:2610.21759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed detection plays a fundamental role in communication-efficient collaborative inference over large-scale networks, where spatially distributed nodes must cooperate using severely quantized messages due to bandwidth constraints. While low-bit quantization is essential for reducing communication overhead, it can significantly degrade detection performance, particularly when prior knowledge of observation noise is unavailable. To address this challenge, we propose a model-driven deep learning framework for distributed detection with low-bit quantization. For fixed local quantizers, we first derive the exact finite-sensor maximum a posteriori (MAP) detection error and prove that, under conditionally independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) observations, independent local randomizations, and a common quantization-level constraint, identical quantizers preserve the supremum of the average network Chernoff information. Guided by these results, we develop a binary probabilistic quantizer with a trainable neural probability controller and design a tree-structured probabilistic quantizer for scalable multi-bit quantization. The exact finite-sensor MAP error provides the training objective for the binary quantizer, while we derive a computationally tractable Bhattacharyya surrogate objective for training the multi-bit quantizer. For both cases, we derive analytical MAP fusion rules based on the class-conditional probability mass functions (PMFs) of the quantized messages. When the observation statistics are unknown, these PMFs are estimated from held-out labeled data, yielding plug-in MAP detectors. Simulation results show that the proposed method approaches centralized-oracle performance at higher quantization resolutions and remains effective under changes in network size and test-time signal amplitude.
item.dc:creator: Wei Guo, Meng He, Chuan Huang, Hengtao He, Shenghui Song, Jun Zhang, Khaled B. Letaief

item.title: Legitimate Reconstruction Advantage in Wiretapped Semantics-Aware Remote Monitoring
item.description: arXiv:2610.21819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates joint accuracy and security in semantics-aware remote monitoring, where source updates intended for a legitimate receiver may also be intercepted by an eavesdropper. We define legitimate reconstruction advantage (LRA) as the joint event that the intended receiver correctly reconstructs the current source state using received updates while the eavesdropper reconstructs it incorrectly. Source evolution changes the relevance of received updates at the two receivers, so their marginal reconstruction accuracies do not, in general, determine the probability of this joint event. Under randomized stationary (RS) transmission and zero-order-hold reconstruction at both receivers, we derive an explicit joint stationary distribution and closed-form expressions for LRA probability and persistence for general finite-state ergodic Markov sources. For two-state and uniform-transition sources, we obtain algebraic expressions that enable low-complexity optimization of RS policies. Analytical and numerical results show that maximizing the probability of legitimate advantage need not maximize its persistence. For two-state sources, rare-transmission analysis reveals that, at a fixed sum of transition probabilities, greater transition asymmetry can increase persistence while reducing LRA probability. Moreover, optimizing marginal accuracy and security metrics can select policies that are suboptimal for LRA. Counterintuitively, more frequent transmission or improved legitimate-channel reliability can increase legitimate reconstruction accuracy while reducing LRA probability. Finally, a geofencing application translates prescribed LRA requirements into spatial constraints on eavesdropper locations.
item.dc:creator: Bowen Li, Nikolaos Pappas

item.title: Uncertainty-Aware Federated Learning for Joint Communication and Computation in XR Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.21969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The convergence of communication and computation, empowered by artificial intelligence (AI) enhanced capabilities, emerges as a key enabler for realizing the promising functionalities of the sixth-generation of communication systems (6G). To this end, this paper investigates an AI-native, robust network, where multiple base stations (BSs) simultaneously serve several extended reality (XR) devices. The paper then presents an innovative distributed deep learning-based approach to simultaneously manage the transmit and computing powers, and computation allocation, amidst uncertainties in both channel and computing states information. Under such an interference network scenario, the paper proposes a robust approach for minimizing the worst-case delay across the served XR devices, subject to computation and power constraints. The paper leverages a deep neural network (DNN) that can be trained either centrally or in a federated manner to map estimated channels and computation requirements to optimized resource allocations per BS. During training, uncertainty samples, reflecting both channel and computing estimation errors, are injected after the DNN output to account for such joint uncertainties. Our results validate the enhanced robust delay performance and scalability of joint uncertainty injection as compared to uncertainty-agnostic methods and state-of-the-art benchmarks, with federated learning-based solutions achieving near-centralized performance while enhancing efficiency, privacy, and adaptability.
item.dc:creator: Robert-Jeron Reifert, Hayssam Dahrouj, Alaa Alameer Ahmad, Haris Gacanin, Aydin Sezgin

item.title: Design of a Family of Rate-Adaptive LDPC Convolutional Codes with Short Constraint Length
item.description: arXiv:2610.22231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the design of some high-rate, adaptive, low-density parity-check (LDPC) convolutional codes with short constraint length, based on interleaved parity-check polynomials. Starting from some known results regarding the selection of polynomials that yield codes free of short cycles in the associated Tanner graphs, we propose some new constructions based on Golomb rulers, along with relaxed variants that do not strictly satisfy the Golomb ruler condition, but retain similar structural properties. The result is a family of rate-adaptive code constructions with code rates of the form $R=(n_0-1)/n_0$. Conditions for the absence of length-4 cycles are derived, together with upper bounds on the free distance that are met in all considered examples.
item.dc:creator: Massimo Battaglioni, Edoardo Carnevali, Franco Chiaraluce, Marco Baldi, Giovanni Cancellieri

item.title: Minimizing Age of Incorrect Information in Pull-Based Remote Estimation of a Markov Source
item.description: arXiv:2610.22265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider a discrete-time pull-based remote estimation system involving an information source and a remote monitor where the information source is a finite-state irreducible discrete-time Markov chain (DTMC) process. In this system, the remote monitor sends a pull request towards the source which responds by sampling its process so as to transmit the sampled values towards the monitor through a delay channel, encapsulated in information packets. We consider i) zero delay (ZD) and ii) unit delay (UD) channels, where the packet transmission times are zero and one slot, respectively. For remote estimation, we use the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimator, and for quantifying its performance, we use the mean age of incorrect information (MAoII) which is a recently proposed freshness and mismatch metric that penalizes an incorrect estimation along with its duration. Our goal is to obtain pull policies so as to minimize MAoII under a long-run sampling rate constraint. For the ZD model, we propose a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) formulation of the problem, which allows us to find the optimum observation-dependent pull policy. On the other hand, the UD channel prevents the monitor from possessing perfect information on the actual AoII process at any given time, and the SMDP formulation of the ZD channel cannot readily be used for the UD model. For the system with the UD channel, we first provide a numerical algorithm to calculate the MAoII and the average sampling rate for a given observation-dependent pull policy. For the optimization of the underlying remote estimation system, we use the joint distribution of the age and source processes to be obtained from the history of all observations, termed as belief. Subsequently, we propose a belief-dependent policy obtained via the belief-MDP formulation and a constrained deep reinforcement learning (CDRL) algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Ismail Cosandal, Sennur Ulukus, Nail Akar

item.title: The Information Bottleneck is NP-hard
item.description: arXiv:2610.22272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a joint distribution $P_{XY}$ on a finite alphabet, the information bottleneck method seeks a representation $T$ of $X$ that is as informative as possible about $Y$ while compressing $X$, where $T$ and $Y$ are conditionally independent given $X$. We show that computing the optimal value $\mathrm{IB}(P_{XY},R) = \sup_T \{ I(Y;T) : I(X;T) \le R \}$ of the information bottleneck problem, as well as its Lagrangian relaxation $L_{\beta}(P_{XY}) = \sup_T \big[I(Y;T) - \beta I(X;T)\big]$, is NP-hard. Moreover, unless $\mathrm{P} = \mathrm{NP}$, neither $\mathrm{IB}(P_{XY},R)$ nor $L_{\beta}(P_{XY})$ can be approximated in polynomial time within an additive error of order $|\mathcal{X}|^{-3/2}$.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Bruno, Ugo Vaccaro

item.title: When Fresh Information Is Not Enough: Age-of-Actuation-Optimal Scheduling for Energy-Harvesting Actuators
item.description: arXiv:2610.22304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study transmission scheduling in an energy-harvesting actuation system where an actuation requires both a received update and available energy. While age of information (AoI) measures information freshness, age of actuation (AoA) measures the time elapsed since the latest completed actuation. The transmitter observes the receiver's AoA and battery state and decides whether to transmit a fresh update in each slot. We formulate average-AoA minimization as a Markov decision process and establish an AoA-threshold property for an optimal policy. We also derive the average AoA in closed form under the AoI-optimal policy, which is always-transmit. Numerical results show that AoA-aware scheduling can improve actuation freshness while reducing the number of transmissions, although information freshness may deteriorate. The two policies coincide for some pairs of channel success and energy-arrival probabilities. For a one-unit battery, the transmission rate under the AoA-optimal policy can vary nonmonotonically with the energy-arrival probability.
item.dc:creator: Ali Nikkhah, Anthony Ephremides, Nikolaos Pappas

item.title: Defining and Generating Compositional Structure
item.description: arXiv:2610.20922v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Compositional structure is pervasive in nature and across scales: atoms combine into molecules, molecules into cells, and cells into organisms, while further compositional hierarchies appear within each level. More broadly, compositionality, the reuse and recombination of parts into novel structures, is a fundamental source of interesting complexity in both natural and artificial systems. Yet despite its importance, and despite our apparent ease in recognizing it, mathematical accounts capturing what we intuitively mean by compositional structure remain limited. Here, we fill this gap by formalizing a simple idea: compositional structure emerges when parts, considered together, reveal shared structure that is not captured when those parts are modeled separately. We express this idea using algorithmic information theory, the mathematics of information and compression, which provides a natural way to identify structure in arbitrary data without specifying in advance what that structure must look like. Applied across scales, our definition informs where and how compositional structure emerges within an object. Using tractable approximations, we then invert the framework to generate compositional objects: we specify the desired form of their compositional structure without prescribing their particular content, and optimize directly over strings and images. The resulting objects exhibit readily recognizable hierarchical reuse and part-whole organization, suggesting that the definition captures compositional structure rather than merely complexity, regularity, or shared information. Finally, we discuss implications for machine learning, including a new perspective on depth in neural architectures and principles for constructing compositional data curricula capable of supporting open-ended learning.
item.dc:creator: Eric Elmoznino, Tejas Kasetty, Blaise Ag\"uera y Arcas, Yoshua Bengio, Guillaume Lajoie

item.title: Efficient Agnostic Learning of Univariate Densities Under Local Differential Privacy
item.description: arXiv:2610.21033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a general framework for non-interactive locally differentially private (LDP) learning of structured univariate distributions that can be approximated by piece-wise polynomials. This gives the first sample-efficient LDP learners for several distribution classes, including mixtures of log-concave distributions, such as Gaussian mixture models (GMMs). These learners also provide agnostic guarantees and are computationally efficient. We also prove a lower bound for learning GMMs under LDP, improving on the standard pure-DP packing lower bounds of Bun et al. [BKSW19]. To obtain our general learning framework, we develop an efficient non-interactive LDP algorithm for synthetic data generation over large domains, which may be of independent interest. We then use it together with a deterministic adaptation of the non-private piecewise polynomial learner of Acharya et al. [ADLS17].
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Afzali, Hassan Ashtiani, Sivan Sabato

item.title: Multiplicative Semidefinite Programming Upper Bounds on Quantum No-Signalling-Assisted Zero-Error Capacity
item.description: arXiv:2610.21071v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study zero-error communication and exact simulation of quantum channels assisted by quantum no-signalling correlations. For a channel with Kraus operator space $K$, we introduce a semidefinite programming parameter $\Gamma(K)$ that is exactly multiplicative under tensor products and upper-bounds $\Theta_{\rm NS}(K)$, where $\log_2\Theta_{\rm NS}(K)=C_{0,\rm NS}(K)$ and $C_{0,\rm NS}(K)$ denotes the asymptotic quantum no-signalling-assisted zero-error capacity. Among known upper bounds on $\Theta_{\rm NS}$ given by semidefinite programs, $\Gamma$ is the tightest. We also prove that the previously introduced simulation lower bound $\Sigma^{-}(K)$ is exactly multiplicative and satisfies $\Theta_{\rm NS}(K)\leq\Gamma(K)\leq\Sigma^{-}(K)\leq\Gamma(K)^2$. Using this multiplicativity, we show that neither $S_{0,\rm NS}(K)=\log_2\Sigma^{-}(K)$ nor its regularized extension $S_{0,\rm NS}(K)=\lim\nolimits_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\log_2\Sigma^{-}(K^{\otimes n})$ holds in general. This answers an open question about the asymptotic simulation cost $S_{0,\rm NS}(K)$. For classical-quantum channels, we obtain sharp bounds. If $r$ is the effective output dimension, then $\Theta_{\rm NS}\leq\Gamma\leq(1+r^{1/2})\Theta_{\rm NS}/2$ and $\Gamma\leq\Sigma^{-}\leq(1+r^{1/2})\Gamma/2$. If $k$ is the minimum rank of the output support projections, then $\Sigma^{-}/\Theta_{\rm NS}\leq[(1+r^{1/2})/(1+k^{1/2})]^2$, and this bound is sharp for every $1\leq k\leq r$. Thus, we obtain the sharp bound $S_{0,\rm NS}-C_{0,\rm NS}\leq2\log_2[(1+r^{1/2})/(1+k^{1/2})]$.
item.dc:creator: Xin Li, Yinan Li

item.title: A One-Sided McDiarmid-Type Inequality for Heavy Tails via Reverse KL Tensorization
item.description: arXiv:2610.21103v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We revisit McDiarmid's inequality, a central tool in statistical learning theory and algorithm analysis. We show that large deviations above the mean are exponentially unlikely for functions of independent random variables that are almost surely bounded above and satisfy a conditional moment assumption of order $p\in(1,2]$. When $p<2$, the result applies even when the function has infinite variance. Our proof relies on a new tensorization inequality for the Kullback--Leibler divergence, termed reverse KL tensorization, which may be of independent interest. Applications include concentration of the sample mean and median-of-means estimator, and one-sided uniform risk bounds for unbounded losses.
item.dc:creator: Hanuka Eshima, Amedeo Roberto Esposito, Andrea Paudice

item.title: Optimal Reduced Representatives of Quadratic APN Permutations in Odd Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.21169v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The formal derivative of the reduced polynomial representative of a map on a binary finite field depends on the coordinates, although its differential uniformity does not. This matters for lifting permutations to Galois rings: a polynomial over a Galois ring of characteristic a power of two greater than two permutes the ring exactly when its reduction permutes the residue field and the derivative of the reduction has no zero there. We prove that for every odd $n\ge5$, every quadratic almost perfect nonlinear permutation $Q$ of $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}$ admits invertible binary-linear maps $L$ and $A$ such that the derivative of the reduced representative of $L\circ Q\circ A$ has no zero and each of its nonempty fibres has exactly two elements. The range is exact: this fails for $n=3$, as computed earlier, and for even $n$ there are no such permutations. For $n\ge9$, a linearization and a projectively injective cofactor map reduce the problem to counting binary matrices: more than 5% of the invertible inputs $A$ succeed, more than half for $n\ge15$, without any classification. For $n=5,7$ we use two independent classifications and finite certificates. Consequently every such permutation is linearly equivalent to a counterexample to the reduced critical-point conjecture of Bartoli and St\u{a}nic\u{a} that lifts to permutation polynomials of optimal differential uniformity over every Galois ring with this residue field. For odd $n\ge9$ the existence proof is checked in the Lean 4 proof assistant.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Fukui

item.title: Explicit reduced APN permutations: ramification and optimal Galois-ring lifts
item.description: arXiv:2610.21178v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $m\ge5$ be odd and $q=2^m$. For every odd $r$ with $3\le r<m$ and $\gcd(r,m)=1$ we give the reduced polynomial $P_{m,r}=\mathrm{red}((T_r^3)^{2^{m-2}})$, $T_r=\sum_{i<r}X^{2^i}$, explicitly: it has coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_2$ and exactly $3r-2$ terms, it is an APN permutation of $\mathbb{F}_q$, and its formal derivative $1+X^{2^{r-2}}+X^{2^{m-2}}$ has no zero on $\mathbb{F}_q$ and is two-to-one. We determine the ramification of $P_{m,r}$ as a map of the projective line for all admissible $(m,r)$: there are $2^{m-r}$ finite ramification points, all wild, with index and different exponent $2^{r-2}$, all over the single finite branch value $1$. The $0/1$ lift of $P_{m,r}$ satisfies an identity in $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ that evaluates it over every Galois ring $\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)$ with $m-1$ squarings, one general multiplication and $r+5$ additions or subtractions. For every quadratic optimal APN permutation $p$ of $\mathbb{F}_q$ (in particular $P_{m,r}$), every $k\ge2$ and every coefficient lift $F$ of $p$ to $\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)$, we determine the differential rows of $F$ exactly in the unit directions whose residue lies outside the kernel $\{0,\rho\}$ of the linear part of $p'$ (they are the residue rows of $p$; $\rho=1$ for $P_{m,r}$) and in the directions in $2^{k-1}\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)\setminus\{0\}$ (every nonzero entry equals $2q^{k-1}$). We also give a self-contained proof of the Li--Wang criterion for a Gold function plus a linearised polynomial, which explains why the inner map of $P_{m,r}$ is not a monomial, and record a two-word, two-layer transition that a simple linear layer forbids at the residue level.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Fukui

item.title: Antenna Placement for Movable Antenna-Enabled Near-Field Target Localization
item.description: arXiv:2610.21191v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) have recently emerged as a promising technology to enhance the wireless sensing performance by exploiting additional spatial degrees of freedom. In this work, we consider an MA-enabled near-field target localization problem under a device-based sensing architecture, where the sensing target actively transmits signals and the sensing receiver estimates its location based on the received signals. We adopt the squared position error bound (SPEB) as the sensing performance metric and aim to minimize the target's SPEB by optimizing the antenna placement at the sensing receiver. The resulting optimization problem is highly non-convex due to the minimum antenna spacing constraints and the intricate dependence of the SPEB on the antenna locations and the intractable form of SPEB. To tackle this problem, we first relax the inter-spacing constraints and accordingly formulate an antenna position distribution problem in terms of degree-4 truncated moments. The reformulated moment-based problem admits an equivalent semidefinite programming formulation and can be optimally solved using standard convex optimization solvers. Using truncated moment theory, we then recover an optimal antenna position distribution supported on a finite number of locations and construct an efficient clustered placement policy. Numerical results demonstrate that the constructed optimal distribution exhibits a three-cluster structure with source-dependent weights. The proposed antenna placement method outperforms conventional array geometries and closely approaches the exhaustive-search benchmark scheme.
item.dc:creator: Jinjian Liu, Xianxin Song, Xianghao Yu

item.title: Finite-History Outage Certification for Partially Observed Fluid Antenna Receivers
item.description: arXiv:2610.21252v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fluid antenna receivers can select a service position from partial port observations, but finite historical data leave uncertainty in the covariance used for that decision. We develop deployment-before-use reliability certification for a frozen partial-observation rule. A proper predictive density defines a history-based parameter region. Gaussian covariance envelopes, shared conditional-probability bounds and selector enclosures provide simultaneous risk bounds over continuous parameters and discontinuous port decisions. Separate history-coverage and integration budgets limit erroneous positive certification to 0.05 for a single qualification procedure under the stated stationary model and numerical assumptions. Confidence-set inclusion allows a new independent history to reuse the risk computation with the rule unchanged. In a structured Gaussian example with 32 candidate positions, five noisy probes and target outage 0.001, all 282 risk groups are qualified; the largest upper bound is 0.000999748. A separate coupled comparison gives a current-rule outage interval of $[7.6820,9.1266]\times10^{-4}$ and resolves lower outage than two observed-port controls using the same historical fit. One independently recalibrated history reuses the certificate without additional risk sampling. Unresolved and adverse-member controls delimit this reuse.
item.dc:creator: Yuanjun Shen

item.title: The Rate of the Delsarte Bound for Binary Codes and Spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.21263v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give the asymptotic rate of Delsarte's linear programming bound for binary codes and spherical codes. This extends previous work of the author which formulated and proved an analogue of the conjecture of Afkhami-Jeddi, Cohn, Hartman, de Laat, and Tajdini for binary codes, obtaining the rate of the Delsarte linear program at distance $1/2-1/\pi$. The lower bounds introduce ideas from potential theory into the study of Delsarte's bounds, whereby the measures underlying a system of orthogonal polynomials give an obstacle problem. We solve the resulting obstacle problem in the case of binary codes and spherical codes, obtaining a closed form for the lower bound in terms of elliptic integrals. For the upper bounds, we relate the $N$-qubit construction for binary codes used in previous work of the author to the constructions in OpenAI's Chapter 2 for spherical codes and observe that they both involve interlacing spectra. This leads to a variational problem involving measures constructed from these spectra under the Markov-Krein correspondence. This variational problem admits an exact solution and matches the lower bound.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Salmon

item.title: Parallel Repetition for Entangled Games via Conditional Relative Entropy
item.description: arXiv:2610.21410v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a proof of the cubic parallel-repetition bound for finite two-player entangled games using quantum conditional relative entropy. For a game with entangled value $1-\varepsilon<1$ and answer alphabets $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$, its $n$-fold repeated value is at most \[ \exp[-\Omega(\varepsilon^3n/L)],\qquad L:=\max\{1,\log(|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|)\}, \] for every $n\ge1$. This recovers Song's cubic rate. We also prove a threshold bound: the probability of winning a fraction at least $1-\varepsilon+\delta$ is at most $\exp[-\Omega(\delta^5n/(\varepsilon^2L))]$ for $0<\delta\le\varepsilon$. Our information charge is the decrease in relative entropy when a question reference is discarded. Our comparison states preserve the original conditional question law. A chain rule bounds the coordinate charges using the cost of conditioning on checked wins and retaining checked answers. Our main lemma converts small charges into nearby pure-state descriptions and local corrections, each depending only on one player's question. Together with Song's sampler, these enable approximate local preparation of the conditioned workspace.
item.dc:creator: Rahul Jain

item.title: Decoding Failure Biases IBLT Count Measurements: A Gaussian-Selection Law at the Peeling Threshold
item.description: arXiv:2610.21418v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a self-sizing set-reconciliation protocol, a small first-round Invertible Bloom Lookup Table (IBLT) sketch attempts peeling decoding; after failure, the protocol estimates the difference count $d$ from the count energy and sizes the second round from a lower quantile of the measurement. This quantile must be computed conditionally on failure: the measurement and peeling success are determined by the same random mapping, so conditioning can shift the measurement law. In the ideal peeling model, inside the critical window where failure has nondegenerate probability, the standardized energy and a statistic of the unsigned mapping that governs the peeling outcome (the precritical score) have a joint Gaussian limit with correlation $\eta_k\rho^2$, $\rho$ being the sign imbalance and $\eta_k$ a closed-form constant. The measurement conditional on failure is thus a bivariate normal truncated to a half-plane, which we call the Gaussian-selection law. Since $\eta_k$ changes sign between $k=4$ and $k=5$, under one-sided imbalance the unconditional threshold undercovers exactly when $k\ge5$ and is conservative for $k=3,4$. The key tool is a quenched CLT for a signed quadratic form on a random overlap graph; under asymptotically balanced signs, conditioning on any unsigned mapping event that is permutation-invariant and has probability bounded away from zero leaves the standard normal limit unchanged. After failure the protocol observes the total sign; inverting the selection law yields an upper confidence bound for $d$, asymptotically conservative in the critical window and, when $d/\sqrt M\to\infty$, along the whole load axis. The experiments use analytic constants, none fitted; the unconditional threshold carries a selection error that does not vanish with scale, while the corrected selection-law threshold matches per-configuration empirical quantiles.
item.dc:creator: Min Wu

item.title: Controlled-Memory Identification with Shared Generators: Dimension--Horizon Tradeoffs and Quantum--Classical Separation
item.description: arXiv:2610.21797v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the finite-horizon identification limits of a \(d\)-dimensional memory when the control interface is restricted to four shared, time-homogeneous generators. A writer encodes a message by applying a prefix word to a common root state. The verifier then applies a candidate-dependent query word followed by a shared terminal binary test, with each word of length at most \(T\). For fixed error tolerances \(\lambda_2>0\) and \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2<1\), the optimal identification sizes satisfy \(\ln N_{\mathsf Q,4}=\Theta_{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}(\min\{d^2,T\})\) for arbitrary CPTP generators and \(\ln N_{\mathsf S,4}=\Theta_{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}(\min\{d,T\})\) for stochastic maps. Four unitary letters and four permutation letters attain these respective bounds, showing that a four-letter reversible alphabet reaches the static code-size orders in optimal quadratic and linear word length. In the fully dimension-limited regime, this yields \(\ln N_{\mathsf Q,4}=\Theta(d^2)\) versus \(\ln N_{\mathsf S,4}=\Theta(d)\), establishing a quadratic quantum--classical separation in logarithmic code size. Low-overlap Grassmann and agreement-code packings supply the orbit endpoints, while exact inverse query words match each encoded state to its designated test. At the sharp boundary \(\lambda_2=0\), \(0\leq\lambda_1<1\), all four model classes satisfy \(\ln N=\Theta(\min\{\ln d,T\})\). Thus any fixed positive false-acceptance tolerance activates the metric-packing regime, whereas zero false acceptance imposes an exclusive-witness constraint and yields the logarithmic-dimension boundary.
item.dc:creator: Yixin Zhao

item.title: On Minimum Divergence for Distribution Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2610.21872v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the possibility of generalizing maximum-entropy reconstruction, which approximately recovers a probability distribution from finitely many (generalized) moments by minimizing the Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence to a reference measure. The reconstruction lies in an exponential family and is also the best KL approximation of the unknown distribution within that family: moment matching and information projection coincide. Replacing KL by a smooth f-divergence, the reconstruction still exists in an associated family, but the best approximation property does not. Specifically, a family is called entropy-adapted if the projection of any distribution matches its moments. We show that, up to equivalence, KL is the only $C^2$ f-divergence that is entropy-adapted, whatever the choice of the generalized moments. We illustrate the consequences of this failure numerically.
item.dc:creator: Justin Bec, Thomas Le Corre, Aur\'elien Garivier

item.title: One generation of the Standard Model as a quantum error-correcting code
item.description: arXiv:2610.21879v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Together with a right-handed neutrino, the fermions of one generation of the Standard Model are labelled by five bits, a combinatorial structure tied to anomaly cancellation. We make this precise. Anomaly cancellation is the vanishing of a cubic form, the defining property of triorthogonal codes, the quantum error-correcting codes behind magic state distillation. Removing the right-handed neutrino gives a $[[15,1,3]]_p$ code for every prime $p$, including the Bravyi-Kitaev code for $p = 2$. For qutrits it is the unique shortest distance-three triorthogonal code.
item.dc:creator: Shiroman Prakash, K. L. Ramya

item.title: Differentially Private Distribution Release of Gaussian Mixture Models via KL-Divergence Minimization
item.description: arXiv:2506.03467v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) are widely used statistical models for representing multi-modal data distributions, with numerous applications in data mining, pattern recognition, data simulation, and machine learning. However, recent research has shown that releasing GMM parameters poses significant privacy risks, potentially exposing sensitive information about the underlying data. In this paper, we address the challenge of releasing GMM parameters while ensuring differential privacy (DP) guarantees. Specifically, we focus on the privacy protection of mixture weights, component means, and covariance matrices. We propose to use Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence as a utility metric to assess the accuracy of the released GMM, as it captures the joint impact of noise perturbation on all the model parameters. We develop a KL-divergence-driven optimization framework for differentially private GMM release that jointly designs privacy-budget allocation and parameter perturbations. Through theoretical analysis, we quantify the effects of privacy budget allocation and perturbation statistics on the DP guarantee, and derive a tractable expression for evaluating KL divergence. We formulate and solve an optimization problem to minimize the KL divergence between the released and fitted non-private models, subject to a given $(\epsilon, \delta)$-DP constraint. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves strong privacy guarantees while maintaining high utility.
item.dc:creator: Hang Liu, Anna Scaglione, Sean Peisert

item.title: Direction-Shift Keying for High-Mobility mmWave Communications: Geometry-Based Resilience to Short Channel Coherence Times and Phase Noise
item.description: arXiv:2509.01103v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Communication reliability in high-mobility millimeter-wave (mmWave) systems is fundamentally challenged by rapid channel variations, manifested in short channel coherence times, and phase noise, which necessitate frequent channel estimation and phase tracking. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Direction-Shift Keying (DSK), a geometry-based modulation scheme that exploits the relative stability of propagation directions rather than the rapidly varying amplitude and phase of the wireless channel. DSK conveys information through distinguishable directions of arrival (DoAs), enabled by a distributed antenna system (DAS), thereby shifting the communication principle from channel-dependent to geometry-dependent signaling. We first derive the structure of the optimal DSK detector for a mobile device equipped with an arbitrary number of antennas. We then establish the fundamental law governing the temporal stability of propagation directions, termed Direction Coherence Time (DCT), and show that DCT scales as $d/v$, where $d$ is the transmitter--receiver distance and $v$ is the relative velocity. In contrast, conventional Channel Coherence Time (CCT) scales as $\lambda/v$, where $\lambda$ denotes the wavelength, revealing a coherence-time advantage on the order of $d/\lambda$, potentially exceeding four orders of magnitude in mmWave systems. Furthermore, we establish the inherent invariance of DSK to common phase rotations, providing resilience to common oscillator phase noise without explicit phase tracking. Numerical results corroborate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the potential of geometry-based signaling for reliable high-mobility mmWave communications.
item.dc:creator: Mohaned Chraiti, Ozgur Ercetin, Ali Ghrayeb, Ali Gorcin

item.title: Coverage Region Analysis and Optimization of FIRES-Assisted NOMA and OMA Systems
item.description: arXiv:2511.01111v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fluid integrated reflecting and emitting surfaces (FIRES) are investigated. In these metasurfaces, each subarea hosts an active element capable of simultaneous transmission and reflection, phase, and geometric positioning control within the subarea. We develop a coverage-centric system model for the two-user downlink scenario (one user per half-space) under spatially correlated Rician fading and imperfect phase control. First, we derive closed-form far-field line-of-sight (LoS) coverage bounds that reveal the effects of aperture size, base station (BS) distance, transmit power, energy-splitting (ES), and phase errors. Protocol-aware corollaries are then presented for both orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), including conditions for successful successive interference cancellation (SIC). Second, we formulate coverage maximization as a bi-level optimization problem consisting of (i) an outer search over FIRES element positions, selecting one active preset per subarea under minimum-spacing constraints, and (ii) an inner resource allocation problem tailored to the multiple-access scheme, which is one-dimensional for OMA and a small convex program for NOMA. The proposed framework explicitly accounts for target rate constraints, ES conservation, power budgets, geometric placement limits, and decoding-order feasibility. Extensive simulations demonstrate that FIRES, by jointly exploiting geometric repositioning and passive energy control, substantially enlarges the coverage region compared with a conventional simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS) under the same element budget. Furthermore, NOMA yields additional coverage gains when feasible. The analytical coverage bounds closely match the simulation results and quantify the robustness of FIRES to phase-control imperfections.
item.dc:creator: Farshad Rostami Ghadi, Kai-Kit Wong, Masoud Kaveh, Hanjiang Hong, Chan-Byoung Chae, Lajos Hanzo

item.title: Novel Inconsistency Results for Partial Information Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2512.16662v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that three cornerstone properties of classical information theory, namely non-negativity of information, the chain rule, and invariance under invertible transformations, become mutually incompatible when extended to Partial Information Decomposition (PID), the framework for decomposing the information that multiple sources carry about a target into redundant, unique, and synergistic contributions. This is, to our knowledge, the first PID incompatibility result involving only direct extensions of standard information-theoretic principles, without relying on any PID-specific assumptions. It reveals that PID necessarily operates in a different conceptual realm from classical information theory, where not all familiar properties can be preserved. Additionally, we re-examine the incompatibility result of Rauh et al. involving the so-called identity property and show that it holds under weaker assumptions than originally stated. Our proofs leverage the recently developed mereological framework for PID that makes the structural origins of these incompatibilities transparent and allows the results to be formulated for any PID-inducing concept, not just redundant information. We discuss the implications of these findings and examine which of the incompatible properties might be relaxed.
item.dc:creator: Philip Hendrik Matthias, Abdullah Makkeh, Michael Wibral, Aaron J. Gutknecht

item.title: Performance Analysis of Pinching Antenna Systems Enabled NOMA Communications
item.description: arXiv:2604.25285v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) have the advantages in the perspective of flexible antenna reconfiguration, line-of-sight (LoS) creation, and scalability features. To highlight the ascendancy of PASS, we survey the integration of PASS into non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) networks. The locations of nodes are randomly distributed within a circular coverage region. The influencing factors of LoS and none-line-of-sight (NLoS) propagation links from PASS to non-orthogonal nodes are taken into consideration. To characterize performance of PASS-NOMA, we deduce the outage probability and ergodic data rates expressions of two nodes over LoS/NLoS fading channels. In light of these theoretical results, the formally unbounded diversity gains are also characterized with node n under ideal successive interference cancellation (ISIC) and node f over LoS links, when the SNR exceeds a finite threshold. The slopes of ergodic data rate for node n with ISIC equals to one and that of node f presents a zero slope. In addition, the PASS-NOMA system throughput are evaluated in different transmission modes. It is shown from the numerical results that: 1) The outage behaviors of PASS-NOMA networks under LoS/NLoS conditions outperform that of PASS aided orthogonal multiple access (OMA) networks and that of conventional antenna systems (CASS) aided OMA/NOMA networks; 2) The employment of PASS enables the larger ergodic data rates relative to PASS-OMA and CASS-OMA/NOMA networks; and 3) As the quantity of communication radius and PASS' height rises, the performance of PASS-NOMA networks are declined at a certain extent.
item.dc:creator: Xinwei Yue, Xinglun Tao, Jingjing Zhao, Xianfu Lei, Yuanwei Liu, Zhiguo Ding

item.title: Z-Opt: A Near-Optimal Reduced-Complexity Two-Dimensional Grassmannian Constellation
item.description: arXiv:2605.04545v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Grassmannian constellations achieve the capacity of noncoherent communications over Rayleigh fading channels at high SNR, yet their efficient construction remains challenging. In this paper, we present two construction methods for Grassmannian constellations on G(2,1), termed S-Opt and Z-Opt, and propose two low-complexity detectors. Both construction and detection are performed on the unit sphere, known as the Bloch sphere in quantum computing. Exploiting the proportionality between the chordal distance on the Grassmann manifold and the Euclidean distance on the Bloch sphere, we derive a theoretical upper bound on the minimum chordal distance from the Fejes-Toth bound. The S-Opt constellation is constructed from sphere-packing solutions and achieves the theoretical limit corresponding to the considered optimal Bloch-sphere packings. The S-Opt detector applies to arbitrary constellations on G(2,1) and requires a number of complex multiplications scaling linearly with the number of receive antennas and logarithmically with the constellation size, and a number of numerical comparisons scaling logarithmically with the constellation size, while achieving the same performance as the GLRT detector. Based on the insight from the S-Opt construction, we further propose the Z-Opt constellation, constructed by stacking regular polygons on the Bloch sphere, whose minimum chordal distance approaches the derived upper bound over the evaluated constellation sizes. The Z-Opt detector requires a number of complex multiplications scaling linearly with the number of receive antennas and a number of numerical comparisons scaling logarithmically with the square root of the constellation size, while achieving the same performance as the GLRT detector for the Z-Opt constellation.
item.dc:creator: Kotaro Shigenaga, Hiroki Iimori, Yuto Hama, Chandan Pradhan, Szabolcs Malomsoky, Naoki Ishikawa

item.title: Recovery Models for Linear Batch Codes
item.description: arXiv:2605.09748v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Various types of recovery algorithms for batch codes have been considered previously, including asynchronous recovery and recovery algorithms arising from Almost Affinely Disjoint (AAD) families. We initiate a systematic investigation of linear batch codes equipped with recovery algorithms. We introduce online and strongly online batch codes, investigate their relations with asynchronous batch codes, and introduce (m,L)-strongly online batch codes, which provide particularly simple recovery algorithms. We then study simple batch codes associated with arbitrary bipartite graphs, obtaining graph-theoretic conditions for such codes and generalizing several known results.
item.dc:creator: Baran D\"uzg\"un, Henk D. L. Hollmann, Ago-Erik Riet, Vitaly Skachek, Vladislav Taranchuk

item.title: Conditioning Strengthens Classical Entropy and Matrix Inequalities: A Submodular Approach
item.description: arXiv:2605.11998v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dembo, Cover, and Thomas (1991) developed an elegant information-theoretic framework for proving determinantal inequalities for positive definite matrices, which relies on the structural inequalities of differential entropy. Submodular functions, which subsume entropy, inherently satisfy these structural inequalities because they obey generalized forms of the fundamental properties of entropy -- a chain rule and the property that conditioning reduces the function's value (under an appropriate definition of conditioning). Applying subadditivity, Han's inequality (1978), and partition subadditivity (i.e., subadditivity over a partition) yields Hadamard's, Sz\'asz's, and Fischer's inequalities, respectively. Furthermore, this framework recovers Ky Fan's inequality (1955), a strengthening of Hadamard's inequality. We highlight a previously unnoticed information-theoretic insight behind this improvement: conditioning yields a tighter upper bound on the joint entropy than the unconditional one. In this paper, we establish conditional strengthenings of Han's inequality and partition subadditivity in the general setting of submodular functions. We derive equality conditions for these strengthened bounds and characterize when they strictly improve their unconditional counterparts. We specialize these results to differential entropy and apply them to establish strengthened versions of Sz\'asz's and Fischer's inequalities. The strengthening of Sz\'asz's inequality recovers Ky Fan's inequality as a special case, and is strictly stronger than the classical Sz\'asz's inequality for any non-diagonal positive definite matrix. We also derive an inequality concerning eigenvalues, which generalizes and strictly strengthens a corresponding eigenvalue inequality of Ky Fan. We provide numerical examples to explicitly illustrate the tightness of our proposed matrix determinantal bounds.
item.dc:creator: Gunank Jakhar, Gowtham R. Kurri, Suryajith Chillara, Vinod M. Prabhakaran

item.title: A Unified Two-Stage Generative Diffusion Framework for Channel Estimation and Port Selection in Multiuser MIMO-FAS
item.description: arXiv:2605.29679v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) have emerged as a promising technology for next-generation wireless systems. However, practical multiuser multiple-input multiple-output FAS (MIMO-FAS) faces two inherently coupled challenges: acquiring accurate high-dimensional channel state information (CSI) from limited RF chains and solving the combinatorial port selection problem, where the effectiveness of the latter highly depends on the result of the former. In this paper, we propose a unified two-stage diffusion framework that formulates the joint task as a maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) inference problem equivalent to maximizing the posterior expected utility of the port selection, and approximates it through two sequential stages. For Stage I, we employ a continuous flow-based diffusion model as a powerful implicit prior for 2D FAS channels and perform approximate posterior sampling via a parallel guided generation scheme, enabling accurate multiuser channel recovery even under severely low sub-sampling ratios. For Stage II, we train a discrete diffusion model on optimal labels computed by exhaustive search to propose a pool of promising port selection candidates. The final selection is then determined by maximizing the empirical posterior expected utility over this pool, followed by a lightweight local refinement. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed framework simultaneously achieves accurate channel estimation and delivers over 90% of the deployed rate of the computationally expensive exhaustive search over the estimated channel, while substantially improving the minimum achievable rate relative to practical cascaded schemes.
item.dc:creator: Erqiang Tang, Wei Guo, Hengtao He, Shenghui Song, Jun Zhang, Khaled B. Letaief

item.title: Extreme Points of the $(0,\delta)$-LDP Polytope with Small Input Size and Arbitrary Output Sizes
item.description: arXiv:2606.09161v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The structure of locally differentially private (LDP) mechanisms can be understood through the geometry of the corresponding privacy polytope. While the extreme points of the \( (\epsilon,0)\)-LDP polytope are well characterized (Kairouz {et al.}, 2014; Holohan {et al.}, 2017), comparatively little is known for the \((\epsilon,\delta)\)-LDP polytope with \(\delta>0\). Recent work (Elangovan and Jog, 2024) has shown that even in the special case \(\epsilon=0\), the \( (0,\delta) \)-LDP privacy polytope exhibits fundamentally different behaviour. In this work, we provide complete characterizations of the extreme points for the low-input-alphabet regime \(k=2\) and \(k=3\) and with arbitrary output alphabet size \(m \). We also identify new extreme mechanisms for larger input alphabet sizes \(k\), of the star configuration type, as introduced by Elangovan and Jog (2024).
item.dc:creator: Supriya Rawat, Myna Vajha, Gowtham R. Kurri, Anand Sarwate

item.title: AirPASS: Over-the-Air Federated Learning via Pinching Antenna Systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.06768v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates over-the-air federated learning (AirFL) in wireless systems where the access point is equipped with a multi-waveguide pinching antenna system (PASS). We adopt the widely studied learning-oriented AirFL formulation, which seeks to maximize the number of selected devices while keeping the aggregation distortion below a prescribed threshold. The resulting joint optimization of device selection, receive beamforming, and pinching-antenna placement is highly nonconvex due to the intricate coupling among these system variables. To address this challenge, we develop AirPASS, an alternating optimization framework with two main components: a homotopy-Riemannian margin-consolidation method for device selection and receive beamforming under a fixed PASS configuration, and a homotopy-assisted geometry optimization method for updating the pinching-antenna positions under fixed selected devices and beamformer.
item.dc:creator: Seyed Mohammad Azimi-Abarghouyi, Christopher G. Brinton

item.title: On the Power Distance Representation of Bregman Divergences
item.description: arXiv:2607.24197v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We express Bregman divergences between parameters as power distances between corresponding weighted points, and investigate several applications of this representation. First, we show that the Bregman closest pair and diameter problems can be reformulated as bichromatic weighted point problems under the power distance. This reformulation enables Bregman nearest and farthest neighbor queries under power distances to be handled in practice through corresponding Euclidean neighbor queries in one additional dimension, after offsetting the weights. Next, we revisit the problem of computing minimum enclosing Bregman balls (Bregman MEBs) and establish their equivalence to double-sided weight power MEBs. We further show that Bregman MEBs can be approximated by relaxing the double-sided weight power MEB problem to its single-sided weight counterpart. We then present two approaches to solving general power MEB problems: An exact algorithm based on the LP-type framework and an arbitrarily accurate approximation scheme based on iterative Frank-Wolfe optimization. Finally, we show that the potential-function lifting transformations used to construct Bregman Voronoi diagrams can be reinterpreted as classical paraboloid lifting transformations applied to the corresponding weighted point sets. This establishes a direct connection between Bregman Voronoi diagrams and power diagrams, further illustrating how Bregman divergences can be represented as power distances.
item.dc:creator: Frank Nielsen

item.title: 3GPP-Compatible Long-Range Sensing for LEO-ISAC: A Window-Grid Processing Framework
item.description: arXiv:2609.30653v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper addresses long-range sensing in bistatic low-Earth-orbit integrated sensing and communication (LEO-ISAC). Conventional OFDM sensing fails in LEO-ISAC because millisecond-scale propagation delays destroy the transmitter--receiver symbol alignment and, with multiple targets, make the receive window longer than the transmitted block. We propose a window-grid (WG) processing framework that exploits the known beam-intersection swath to resolve both problems purely at the receiver, leaving the 3GPP symbol structure unmodified: the swath delay span is folded into cyclic-prefix-sized slices, each handled by one WG. With 103.2 MHz bandwidth at bistatic ranges beyond 640 km, simulations demonstrate meter-level ranging of two targets, and 1000 Monte-Carlo trials over random target--satellite geometries show that, with an ephemeris-based satellite-selection rule, every target is detected with a 90th-percentile range error of 2.4 m.
